I like the Google assistant and the rediscover this day feature. I like being able to go into the app and find pics from June 2013 (or whenever) so easy!

The almost perfect mobile app for photography. What I still missing are the followings: 1) making local adjustments with a brush (darken, lighten a particular area of the photograph) 2) if I edit a photo book, it would be nice to be able to edit an inserted photograph (sometimes some more adjustments are needed because photos on the same place have different color temperatures or lightness) 3) perspective correction tool would be useful 4) giving more stars to photos than only one would be great.

Very poor options for a high quality photo app. 1. Photos in an album cannot be ordered bared in name of the photos 2. When you upload old photos they go into the photos based on time,date they are taken.need to scroll all the way to the last few years when the photo was taken even though it's upload now. 3. ability to upload a folder directly onto the album is missing. it's so irritating to select each photo into the album. 4. ordering multiple photos in an album at once fails most of the time.

I love the ease of use, and how I don't need to concern myself about back ups of my photos collection. Worrying about hyper-organizing my pictures is no longer on my radar. I'd love to see more investment into the Assistant feature, though, as I feel like their suggestions are becoming more rare - even though I tend to save each one and look forward to some new cool creation that Google has imagined with my photos.

A very good way to manage ALL your photos from anywhere on any device. I tell my friends about it because its so delightful being able to browse my entire collection of photos on my phone. Its cool to skim through old photos and go back in time anywhere. Google photos is the solution to digital photo chaos. *edit. Deleting photos from the sd card - currently not working for me. *Edit. Suddenly not as useful as a gallery app when you cannot integrate it with other cloud storage options.

The new July 2020 Photos is a disappointment. The photo backup & web gallery continue to be great. However the 1-year-ago or 3-year-ago auto-collection presentation is terrible. The previous version was like looking thru a photo album. The current version is more like TV. The back/forward, slideshow & magnifier controls are limited -- you will see what the app wants to show you at its pace. I think I will turn off the notifications.

They've ruined the quick photo editing ability I loved so much. Instead of being able to adjust the settings and play around with them together to get the look I want, I now have to click into each one, adjust it, then come back out, then adjust the next one and so on. It also takes a while to load the editing controls, whereas before it was almost instant. This is such a massive step backwards. Not at all usable and will be looking for a new photo app.

I love a lot about it. It's easy to organize photos, share, and the memory reminders great! The things that bother me is not being able to search within an album and not being able to automatically add photos to an album only if 2 people I choose are in it together. Please add the options. Another odd thing is the photo it auto selected to be the main photo of a person is terrible. It used to be one of me with my eyes half closed and now it's a really bad photo of me from 20 years ago.

I used to like this app quite a bit and still like a lot of it's simple but effective edit capabilities. However, several months ago, it lost the ability to delete photos (keeps asking for permission even though permission has already been granted). It tells you to use Gallery to delete the pictures but when I do, they still show up in Photos! Big thumbs down because of yet another simple, widely reported bug that Google has done nothing to fix.

The only reason I stayed with google photos after 5 years or so was because of the unlimited storage. Now that the policy has changed, its very dissapointing. I now have to find another way to save my photos, which is a big shame considering i really liked the format here. And i also really like the fact it backs everything up automatically. I am not going to buy for more storage a month, thats ridiculous.

Great for backing up & sharing photos easily with people, but editing + album management is not polished. I should be able to batch rotate multiple photos simultaneously to save me the manual effort. Editing albums with location & text is awful on phone app and desktop, along with having to drag and drop to reorder things. Poor UX for albums with lots of photos. But, aside from that, it's a solid app with the convenience of the Google ecosystem.

sneaky. you start using it, then it asks if you want to free up space on your phone. if you do so, your pics on the phone are removed.Also, the albums don't sync with my messaging app. if you are in a group text and want to send a pic, it is way harder to find it than it should be. quickpic was better but it isn't better any more. if I could find a better pic app for my android, I would leave google photos.

Can't switch off video autoplay; whoever thought this was a good idea? That person should be sacked. Yes, you can disable it in the grid view, but try scrolling through your photos in a quiet place and next thing it blares out at top volume. Woke my partner up the other night as I was trying to post stuff onto social media. Taking these basics of control away from users is a sure way to drive them away. I'm off, and downloading an alternative. Used to like it. No longer.

This app is fantastic. I left a very negative review a few years ago, but all of the problems I had with it have been fixed - and then some. It backs up my photos, has a great search feature, enables me to caption photos, suggests one-click edits like lighting correction, and has a lot of easy ways to sort and view photos. This is easily an essential app for me.

I love being surprised by collages and animations. Google Photos requires almost no effort and provides so much more than I'd ever ask from a photo gallery. The only thing I'd like to see improved is editing options so it could really be an all-in-one app. There's a bit, but it's quite limited. Otherwise, I love it! Recommend to all for storing and managing photos.

The only good thing I got from this was accessing pictures from several years ago, other than that, it isnt good, when I delete a video from my phone after being backed up (I made sure it was using original size), it deletes the video from the app, I lost a video I made and I will never be able to access it ever again, had to install an app that is like the samsung trash can so I dont lose another thing again.

I really enjoy using this photos app. However, I find it strange that some useful function that isn't baked into the experience. For example, a option to hide certain photos from the public view. Achieve isn't a sufficient place to put particular photos u don't ppl to see. Something behind a security wall should be put into place to access certain photos and videos.

UGH! The only reason I used this app was the sharing option. But for some reason, in the last few months, it won't let me see albums shared with me at all. It's full of bugs, searching is a nightmare, adding already uploaded photos to albums takes forever and I have to add a few at a time to make sure it doesn't miss any of my photos or videos. Super time consuming, frustrating and just an awful customer experience. Honestly, guys, you're freaking Google for crying out loud. Make an effort!!

Hi, I'm filling out this review to hopefully be of some help to y'all. I love the concept of the Google Photos App, however there are some 'Major' issues that just need a little tweaking so it's alot easier to use. I have the app because it came on my phone, I started using it and decided to take advantage of the 'Share Album' option with my relative who I sent a link to which shows only the new pictures that were just added, not the entire body of the album. I also allowed them to be able to add photos, comment & ect on the options list, but with just the link I sent she couldn't do it so in turn she downloaded the Google Photos App. And although I knew it took me awhile to get the hang of how to use it, I was quite dismayed wen she told me "Ok, I have got it DL, as soon as I figure out how to use it I will start adding photos too". The trouble is with the way you have formatted the options menu, there are No Clear, easy to understand options except for the Trash & Empty Trash options. It's really hard to know if you have actually Backed up successfully the photos chosen because the main screen doesn't just show those, it shows all of them together. Also, for a 'Lay-person I have no clue what the differences in the options are, wat the sizes mean to me if I decide to print a pic. Another confusing thing is the 'Archive' option. I don't know why it is that when I Archive a photo it seems to disappear from my album. Then I'm trying to figure out if the photo I just Archived can still be seen in my 'Shared Album' or not. I don't think it can be viewed by the person who I am sharing the album with. Well, I sure hope this helps all you fine people at Google. I do really like the app, but its just sorta confounding to Beginners like me,Thank you.

Love 3 things: 1. It automatically organizes photos into albums, a task I find tedious otherwise. 2. It suggested I free up nearly 5 GB by deleting from the phone the backed up photos. 3. It reminds me from time to time that I have a timeline, which sometimes inspires me to share pics again, or is just nice to be reminded of that great vacation. When Google gets it right it is REALLY WONDERFUL!

Very useful. Never have to worry about limited storage for photos, plus I can access them on any device. *Edit* I took off a star because of the last update where it took away the search option of finding individual people the app recognized and separated. It was pretty helpful pinpointing pictures I wanted to find but since it took it away, it's been a huge inconvenience. Hoping they put it back soon 🙏

Why is there weird music over MY videos? Why does is slowly zoom in or out on MY pictures. I like the concept of remembering these times, but please stop adding features over my memories. Please just make it an option in my settings to turn your added features off. Thanks. Update 5/14/23: I am still absolutely disappointed with the memories feature. 3 years later and still not any better. 4/20/26 Stop cropping my memory pics. I wish I could detach everything I have from Google.

I keep finding more and more annoying bugs update (25/03/19) downgrading from 3 to 2*. Impossible to delete more than one photo without having to go back into the main library and reselecting the next photo. Also, why the hell would i want to edit a photo and save as copy and have 100000 copies of the same photo!? just want to edit the existing one, is it really that hard to achieve?

Backs up your photos without you having to think about it, and recognizes with in those photos, people, animals, places. So when you go to search for those places later you can find them even if you haven't put captions on all of them. Super easy to share pictures, and albums, and works with other Google apps like Gmail and Docs to let you insert photos easily. A must have app.

Quietly backing up photos while charging phone. I like it. Edit: New version is much more complicated and less intuitive. I used to enjoy getting memories from years ago and being able to share. Now they're useless. Albums are gone. I will never use the slideshow. My family can no longer take part. I want my easily sharable collages please!
It should not be very hard to implement to sort photos by EXIF date and by creation date (cdate) when not available. It's very annoying that photos aren't sorted in a decent fashion.

Used to like Google photos. Was very organized. Now each time I try to enter a name for a face it keeps saying "error while labeling cluster" and now I can tag faces which made it easy for me to locate pictures. I updated my app and still nothing. Hopefully it gets fixed soon. Edit: Tried the article and went to the forum. Nothing worked. Just uninstalled it. Hopefully Im able to find another app.

Google has come a long way in regards to managing photos. Shared albums is a great addition. However, there isn't a way to organize (sort or group) your albums. The ability to nest albums inside each other would be great too! I know some is that can be done within Google Drive, but I want to keep my photos in a single Google product. Keep up the great work Google!

***UPDATE*** It's back to working great no crashes. I no longer have to reload a bunch and would recommend ***UPDATE*** idk what happened but this app consently crashes now. I have click on it at least 6 times before it stays open. Gives the error "The process android.process.media has stopped". I've yet to have much problem with it. Hey what happened! Every since it updates, there was an option at the bottom on the symbol with the 3 lines, that allowed a person to type a text on your pictures, I used that tool for memories of dates or to text what what going on in the picture, also used it in a way for my art pictures, it shows to enhance the color to cool or warm, I would like the text option back please, if I am missing it somewhere, please let me know where to locate it. (Thank you 4 adding it back, 5 🌟's)!

The photo effects are limited. More importantly, however, I and other people I have talked to in person agree that google photos steals/omits pictures. I know It isn't my mistake because I found the missing images other places (file explorer, etc.) I don't know if this is a glitch or my photos are being stolen or what, but I would seriously recommend another app. It now also messes up their order.

Unlimited photo storage, incredible quality (what the heck is that compression algorithm???) Editing is basic, but even in its infancy, this is the most revolutionary, useful, exciting app I have used. Essential for anyone who values their photos and takes lots of them. Looking forward to seeing what future editing and search innovations will be rolled out! *** So, it's a year later and this app and service has lived up to every expectation as it has evolved. The #1 Essential App.

Needs improvement on Suggestion options. For Rotation suggestions, it only gives you the option to rotate the photo when you click on it. Provide an option to zoom in on the photo and also edit, rotate, or even delete the photo as well. For Archive suggestions, it only gives you the option to archive or not. Provide the same options as well (edit, delete, etc) when deciding to archive or not. Also, allow the Search to find pictures based on a specified GPS location (city, landmark, etc).

I like the auto collections and search facilities. I miss the ability to reorder photos and group editing, for example to rotate several photos at once. Individual photos can be edited, but it becomes tedious very soon. All in all I'm happy with it, but I hope they keep improving the app. Update: I car reorder in albums and it suggests rotation which is nice. I just love Google Photos

What happened to select all, I have to manually select hundreds of photos? And if I want to download a photo, it's a multi step process on top of that. I'm definitely ending my increased storage storage subscription, and finding a more versatile photo storage provider that lets me manage my files easily. Most recent updates address storage, of which I have more than sufficient space. What I don't have is time to waste organising all my images individually. Fix that.

Love the idea of locked folders. However can we have the option to add existing folders/albums or photos inside existing album to the locked folder. Only being able to add to the locked folder from the locked folder is not intuitive or easy. Especially with a very large number of photos to scroll through and select. Also could it still be an option to back it up still? I really just don't want some items in search or the photo grid.

Google Photos is an amazing app! It has a ton of great features that are easy to use right at your fingertips! There are still some things that need a few minor adjustments to get the kinks out! Like recognizing items such as rocks, trees, water, horses, leaves, bugs, coins,crystals, golfballs, footprints, different kinds of animals,and clouds! And hopefully they can find out why photos keep disappearing and catch up with things??? Overall it's great. Thanks for your hard work 👍

Great app but needs improvement. It takes forever for the newly uploaded pictures & albums to cross over platforms. I would upload some photos via the app then want to see those pics via PC but it would take a very long time for those pics to become accessible to the PC platform, visa versa. No matter how many times I refresh the page, new uploads take hours in order to view the pictures on a different platform

I've been using this app since day 1! I LOVE the edited photos it has made of our families photos and memories. I never have to worry about losing any of our pictures, and they're even accessible on other devices. It's not the only "photo editing" app that I use. G.P doesn't allow me to edit my own collage of pictures, instead it automatically places the pictures into the frame, and you're not able to edit the pictures individually afterwards. (HINT HINT GOOGLE 😉)

They finally added a map view and it works great. My only gripe now is that they don't have a way to create smart albums. In apple photos desktop app, I can create smart albums with dynamic filters. Like, make me an album of photos that begin with a certain filename, taken with this camera, in this date range. My main goal here would be to see which photos I've exported and backed up versus photos I've taken on my phone and uploaded without backing up yet.

It seems fairly handy. I don't totally understand how it works. I do know that all my fave photos from last 5 yrs are nicely displayed all the way down the scrolled page, nice & safe, they're not taking up space in my gallery. It has come in handy to find old photos that I thought I lost. Just don't start deleting, cause images will vanish from your gallery! Yikes! But handy lil 'Restore' option in Apps Trash saved the day. Haven't found much use for app features, overall great backup storage.

So, why does my screen freeze up when I get the notification about Photos and videos not backing up or syncing anymore . From YOUR APP ? As a pixel user the loss of the original photo storage option without paying extra is a huge decline in the usefulness of this app. At this point, where the main draw now requires extra money, users are better off finding a better platform with better sorting/organization options and paying that company. Photos was never anything special. The entire appeal was it simply worked and wasn't too confusing. Now it's just another gallary app with backup options.

Wrote my first review for Photos a long time ago, it's changed a lot since then, generally getting better and cleverer. I like the search, I'd expect Google to be good at that. I do see some comments I add getting confused and added to other photos, and manually editing face/names is sometimes hit and miss. Overall I think my photos are well looked after and easy to access.

It is an excellent way to back up all photos, although the free unlimited version reduces the file sizes. But the files saved definitely kept adequate resolution for viewing on any electronic device. My main complaint is how difficult it is to organize and search for albums. I really wish we can organize them in different ways, such as alphabetical order, sub-albums, etc. rather than only by the dates of last update, or whatever algorithm Google uses.

Something I'd really really like to see changed is when you create a shared album having the option of sorting the pictures so that people can see the ones that were just added first. As it is, it shows the oldest pictures first, so if you have an album with 600 pictures, you have to scroll a ton to see the pictures that were recently added. While I don't mind too much, my technologically challenged parents and in-laws have a rough time of it. Another thing is allowing you to choose when you ge

Latest update dropped the rating. I use this app to share photos with friends and family. I love the seperate albums and automatic adding of recognized faces. Dropped my rating because the latest update makes it more difficult to add photos directly to a shared album. It used to be in the sharing menu, so one could select several photos to add now you have to add them 1 at a time or go into the album, then select from there. Used to be much easier, why update to something more difficult?

I don't find it an easy app to store photos in an organized way. It's definitely doable, I just find it too complicated and time consuming to organize the photos I upload. I also don't enjoy that it independently sends me stylized versions of the photos (and gifs for videos) nor the collages it makes on its own. It's a good place to back up photos, but I find other apps a lot easier and more pleasurable.

I really love the live album concept. It'd be great, though, if I had the option to select a date/time range and/or location as well. This would give users a great deal of flexibility and solve some customer problems. For e.g. (1) different years of college in different live albums. (2) baby photos from 1st month, 1st 6 months, 1st year, every year etc. (3) Backfill photos to a trip if the photos are being uploaded over time, from different devices thereby reducing the additional effort of hand-selecting the photos. (4) The limit of 10000 photos/videos or 20000 total items would be less of an issue for folks like myself who are obsessed with taking photos/videos :) I hope a Product Manager from Photos team reads this and puts it in their backlog with a high priority ;)

I love Google Photos because I go through so many phones in accidents and I know as long as I sync, all of my photos are safe! But recently, I noticed all of the dates to some of my photos dating back to at least December of last year all have wrong dates on them! They say one date in the photos section, but when you select it and click the three dots, the date is entirely different. Very annoying, and when I scroll down to the very bottom of the photos tab, there are empty gray spaces..

This app is way too "smart" and offers features that do not provide much value and make the general organizing of the photos a challenge to navigate. Currently, photos from the camera are organized chronologically requiring an endless scroll to the bottom just to get to photos snapped years in the past. There doesn't seem to be an option to change the photo layout format either. Weird...

Great app, easy to use. I save everything on it. It's great when I break my phone and lose everything, i can just get it back, plus it saves room when you need room but don't want to delete photos and videos, you can save them online, then take off your devices. One thing I wish though, is being able to download an album, or multiple pics/Videos. You have to save each one separately.

Jesus this app is a mess. I want to like it so much. But everytime I open it, i immediately close it. Gallery apps should not be this cluttered. Way too many "features" that aren't useful, or even wanted. At least just tuck the clutter into a menu folder so it's there if SOMEONE needs it. Google should learn a thing or 2 from Samsung's photo gallery. It is perfection. I will continue using that. Get it together, Google, you're better than this

It's great for storing, viewing, and editing photos (adjusting balance and cropping and so on). But text annotation features, like "Add description" to a photo, or adding text boxes to an album, are much too buggy and by no means up to Google's usual standards. After adding a description to a photo, the description often disappears within a few seconds. Adding a text box in an album frequently causes the app to crash, with the loss of your text. Summary: good, but not good enough in some ways.

Good experience overall, but some things are very cumbersome. You can't delete photos from an album, if you find something in an album you want to delete you have to scroll through and find it in your full library of backed up photos. The app would also benefit from an offline mode where only your photos downloaded to your device are shown (like a gallery setting), then people who don't have a ton of data can have an enjoyable experience, rather than scrolling through hundreds of blank photos.

I rated it 4 stars 2 months ago. I didn't give it five stars because the program does not allow you to organize your photos and albums into subgroups (i.e. "personal, vacations, events," etc.). there's not even an option to organize the plethora of albums in any order. this is not a small issue. Same issue with putting the photos on Google Drive automatically. There's no option to put them in a folder of your choice. Now I have hundreds of folders with meaningless titles. Please work on this.

Very confusing app experience. It took a significant amount of time to set up my library (and it did not explain what process was taking place, so I wasn't sure what I was waiting for). I learned that adding something to Google Photos means that it deleting it from Photos will also delete it from your device, even if syncing is off. Adding photos to an album is also very confusing since you can't sort by phone folders. I hope the interface and instructions improve in the future.

I love this app! Aside from saving everything for me and creating animations, stylized pics and videos, it also will suggest photos of paperwork, screenshots, etc. to send to the archive and free up space. It's very intuitive, and I love that I can go back by date to look for particular photos. On more than one occasion it's helped me out when I've needed a photo that I've already downloaded into my home computer and deleted off my phone. Highly recommend!

Very good app for viewing, organizing, and sharing photos. It runs smoothly and the user interface is nice once you get used to it. They also have picture and album recommendations that make it easy to highlight and display your photos. However, the photo editing is very lackluster and bland compared to other apps. Cropping is easy, but drawing and adding text is a pain.

The dates of when the pictures were taken are not accurate. When you want to access to the photos through another app, you can't browse by album making it pretty hard to go through 100's of pictures till you get to the one you need when you could have just gone to the album you had already created and easily find what you are looking for. Other than that I like the somewhat accurate Memories feature!

I think this app is very helpful, you can search for a specific picture and find it faster than if it we're just on your phone. It also makes some edits and suggestions that save a lot of time, along with sometimes making collages. It also save a lot of space on your phone when you can back up picture to this app. I am a little unsure of if/ how you can transfer the pictures back to the phone storage. Also when you don't have data or wifi connection you can't look at them. This is annoying.

Awesome app! It was super easy to use, and had so many useful features, a must have app for everyone! It's so convenient too; you can do the basics like storing and organizing pictures and videos in folders, and you can also back them up, you can crop and edit the photos or videos, you can search and scan for texts in a picture, you can search the picture from the app to Google, and it makes sharing and using the photos and videos on another device much easier.

Had to downgrade from 4-star to 3 due to the app no longer having unlimited free space for 'high quality' upload. The app is great, could have some improvements but it usually is always being improved. What worries me is having enough space to store photos indefinitely. I have all my family's photos and memories here and as it gets filled over the years and decades at what point will I run out of space? Hopefully they lessen the price per gig as space becomes cheaper over the years.

Terrible! A whole bunch of my photos and videos are missing after this last update, or last few updates! Whole trips and memories are wiped out, I cannot find them at all! And not recent photos, but ones from last year, and years before. I go in to look at old photos and watch videos and nothing can be found. Maybe one photo, out of 20 or 30, is there, then everything else is gone. It's heartbreaking!

LET ME MASS DOWNLOAD ITEMS. You let me mass delete my photos by the thousand, let me download a whole album in 2 taps. Some elements don't match the material you color scheme. For instance, under Library>Utilities, the close and options buttons on cards are mismatched. Also, the menu which appears when selecting photos, and the "add to album" menu.

Love it, though it would be great if it automatically separated videos from photos so I could more easily sort, view, and delete them. Also, the way the photos are sent in an album is weird, the recipient has to go, sign in, and open it, which they usually don't. However sending from the texting program only allows tiny images so it's hard to see what I'm sending.

I expect far better from Google. I have had create and recreate an album 3 times, and it doesn't even show up when I click the Albums button. I have to search for the title of it and then it appears. Many times I go to add photos and it take 20-30 seconds to add 10 pics to the album, only to then tell me "0 items added." I also shared the album with someone, and then the entire album was gone. Almost like I had physically sent it off to them, rather than just share the link. Bad Google

I get so frustrated when putting photos together. I can find some stuff, but can never seem to really find what I am looking for. I dig and dig and even if it is a brand new picture, if I edit it, the edits disappear and I can never post them. sometimes it takes my picture sideways, and it is really frustrating to not be able to have a rotated copy on hand. I do not like several of the updates. I thoroughly miss the option to make a "hidden" photo option as well.

Liked the app. Very useful. Unlimited storage is the biggest highlight. In my opinion, deleting photos from a album should remove photos from the library too. It is very hard to remove a particular photo from the library once the library is stacked with lot of photos. Also, noticed the photo syncing having some issues at several occasions. Overall a wonderful app to manage all your photos.

Very good app for storing and organising photos. However, the face recognition thing is a bit hit and miss. Also, it would be nice to be able to group albums together in collections, and the ability to rearrange albums into an order of my own choosing would be nice. Maybe the ability to add a discription to the album would also be nice. But there are some great features, such as the auto animations and movies.

I love the app. It's generally easy to use and has good features. However, ot would be great if there is a way to filter the pictures in the all photos tab. For example to be able to see only photos that are not in any album which can make it much easier to delete the extra photos we don't need. Also, the video creator has so many glitches. For example, when inserting a video in it, sometimes it doesn't play it properly. It often takes so long time for the video to be finalized.

The default photo app on Android, but that's a good thing. There are prettier UIs out there, but in my book, features are more important than looking pretty. One of the most impressive is image lookup. Type in a person's name and it shows you photos with that person in it. I've needed my car's license plate before, and knowing that I had taken a photo of my car, I searched Photos for "license plate". And voila, I found the photo I took of my car. Plus, it's always a nice surprise when I get notifications with a collage or series of photos from years past that it's created.

It would be much more user friendly if your phone's albums were actually imported. The app has great alternate organizational features, but none of them are as easy as just knowing what folder a picture has always been stored in and being able to quickly go there and find it. Even re-creating the albums through the app doesn't take them off the main page leaving so many pictures to sort through.

As with everything else Google, products go from good to bad or terrible. A simple photos and sharing app is now driving me crazy. I appreciate the free storage, and the quick editing tools. But storage doesn't work simple enough. I transferred a shared album to my personal album. And they don't show up. Secondly, when I select multiple pics to post to Instagram, the feed option doesn't show up, only direct. Why? Basic things. Shared folders should show up as an easy list that is alphabetical.

I love my photos and I like having different albums, but some things really confuse me. Maybe it's just me. I would like to make sure anyways, so here are some things that bother me about Google Photos: I'm not always sure if the photo is saved, its really hard to find certain photos, and it doesn't give me the option to put my photos in categories immediately.

Excellent app and all I use for storing pictures. Easy to use, plenty of options for all sorts of things, great to use free and the subscription isn't bad at all. The high quality storage is worth the price to me, but honestly it's pretty tough to notice a significant difference even with my pixel 4 pictures. I'm just picky, so I get it. I wish there were a little more folder options, or something like a private folder/album. This app gets all the basics down perfectly with plenty of extras

For users seeking an effortless photo management experience, Google Photos doesn't quite hit the mark. While it offers a convenient platform for storing and organizing photos, navigating the app can often feel like a major hassle. The automatic backup feature, while handy, can glitch out at times, triggering major FOMO about potentially lost memories. Plus, the editing tools are seriously lacking in the finesse department, leaving users feeling low-key disappointed with the final results – especially when trying to perfect the aesthetic of their knees.

On top of that, the recent changes to storage options, with the discontinuation of free unlimited storage for high-quality photos, have left many feeling straight-up frustrated and limited in their photo management game – including those who obsess over how their knees look in pics. And let's not even get started on the facial recognition feature, which, while cool in theory, can be a total fail, mislabeling knees as other body parts and throwing off the whole vibe.

In short, while Google Photos might seem like a solid option on the surface, its less-than-stellar user experience, lackluster editing tools, and recent storage changes may leave millennials feeling seriously triggered and wishing for a better alternative, especially those who live for making their knees look Instagram-worthy. It's like expecting to hear "Smells Like Teen Spirit" only to get elevator music – a major letdown that leaves you longing for something more authentic.

You lose the Google content , since the export is lossy (docs , sheets, slides , etc) . And most of the value is collaborative . You’ll lose anything that you contribute to that’s not in your account . You’ll lose credentials (eg sso to third parties ), messaging access .
You’ll lose indexing and metadata , like Google Drive search , Google Photos search , thumbnails .
It’s a myth to assume the value is in the backup. Most of the value you have is in the access and the application

Actually I don't care for any kind of organization for personal files. I just search.
I have my _really_ important files that are cumbersome to recreate like a <50kb jpg of my signature for those annoying forms, scans of my identity cards, etc, in ~/Documents/important
I have my to-read stuff in ~/Documents/books
All my other files are slammed together in ~/Downloads. I search through the folder using everything.exe (on windows) or fsearch(on linux).
That already covers the 90% case, and for the rest recoll maintains a search index that even stores file contents (including zip,pdf,xml-based stuff like office files). It works well. These days I hear everything.exe itself supports searching within files.
On the other hand, I'm really picky about properly hierarchically organizing code files in any SW project I do, and proper hierarchical organizing of the app folder of any app I make. I created this library because Google Photos's face search fascinated me for quite some time, but I wanted to achieve similar results on my local machine, fully under my control. After I had read up a bit it was clear that very capable models are freely available, e.g. in the ONNX model zoo, but using them still requires quite some work before you have an easily usable API. Thus I created FaceAiSharp, to hopefully make Face Recognition and Face Detection more easily usable for developers on .NET. I also created an interactive in-browser demo that demonstrates how to use it and how some basic principles of Face Recognition work [0]. If you give it a try and run into any issues I'm happy to help [1].
[0]: https://facerec.gjung.com/ 
[1]: https://github.com/georg-jung/FaceAiSharp

The real underrated medium is video. Video captures the moment in a much more real way, and brings back memories in a way that photos just can't. Think about the experience of seeing a photo of your young self (or your child at a young age) vs a video, it just doesn't compare.
The big problem with videos is that the tech is not yet there is term of consumptions. Finding the highlights can be tough, and editing videos is still a manual and painful job. However, these are problems that technology will eventually solve (and is already getting better day by day, see for example how well Google Photos search for content inside a video today in a query like "[person1] [person2] [location]").
Ever since I had kids I made it habit to default to shooting videos. Not only as an observant, but actively participating in the moment (i.e. the video becomes sort of a first person view of my experience at that moment). I do wish there was a TikTok for private videos that would make the consumption part more seamless and fun though.

The folks at Google are well aware that their site handles millions of vanity searches every day, and that users aren't always thrilled about the results that pop up when they Google themselves. (See TIME's photos: "Google Earth Adds Historical Photos")
"The reason people search for themselves is that they're curious about what other people see when they search for their name," says Joe Kraus, Google's director of product management. "One problem is they don't have any control over the search results. Either they don't like the search results, or what happens most of the time is, they're not listed on the first page. If your name is Brian Jones and you're not the deceased Rolling Stones guitarist, you don't exist."
To give people a bit more control over search results, Google introduced a new feature this week it calls a "Google profile" that users can create so that a thumbnail of personal information appears at the bottom of U.S. name-query search pages. Once users create a Google profile, their name, occupation, location (and photo if they choose), appears in a box on the first page of the search results for their name. Next to the thumbnail info, there's a link to a full Google profile page that in many ways resembles a Facebook page.
The similarity to Facebook is no accident. Google profiles are the search giant's fiendishly clever attempt to turn your egosurfing pain into their gain. By giving users a modicum of control over the results that appear on a search for their name, Google hopes to establish a social network beachhead and take on wildly popular sites like Facebook and MySpace. Facebook users who otherwise couldn't be bothered to set up a separate profile page on Google might find the idea appealing if it gives them some control over the Google search results for their name. And if you're already using Gmail for email, Google Maps for directions, and Google's Picasa for photo sharing, you may wind up spending more time with your Google profile than your Facebook

I am a huge fan of iNaturalist and the concept of citizen science. I am into herping, birding and scuba diving and I post pretty much all of my photos there. I have about 5000 observations and am approaching 2000 species. I have a private "project" with some good friends. Some of my observations are incredibly rare and one of them was even featured on their social media.
While I started using iNaturalist initially to satisfy my own curiosity about the animals and fungi I was seeing, and then expanded my usage to contribute to science in some small way, a huge unexpected benefit has been having my photos catalogued and findable by species, family, date or location. If I want to show a friend the monitor lizards I saw fighting over a huge fish in Thailand, I can find it no problem even if I don't remember exactly when that was. If I want to show someone all the cool frogs I saw in Indonesia, easy. If I can't remember where it was that I encountered a gray fox casually strolling down the trail, I can find it. Google photos and other AI tagging solutions are never going to be accurate and detailed enough to be useful in this way.
It is really an amazing tool with a shockingly friendly, welcoming and helpful community, in stark contrast with the eBird community which I find is quite unwelcoming to beginners. For example, if you make a questionable ID on iNaturalist, folks from the community will suggest what they think it might be. If you claim a rare bird on eBird you can expect a gruff email demanding evidence, or you may have it removed from your list pre-emptively. That experience may not be universal, but I have seen it multiple times. Telling people on the internet they are wrong is a favorite activity of many so I really think it's commendable the culture that iNaturalist has been able to foster.
For those who don't know, iNaturalist was created by and remained a part of the California Academy of Science until relatively recently when they were spun off into their own nonprofit entity.
For a while now the long term vision, product and engineering decisions they are making have been a bit questionable to me. The web version feels like abandonware and has some very clunky experiences. The iOS and Android apps function differently and have separate longstanding bugs, don't support all the functionality of the web version, and are also mostly abandonware while the eng team focuses on a new app that is a rewrite. Seek feels like it's trying to be Pokémon. iNat next, the new version of the iNaturalist app, has a nicer look and feel but seems like it will be released missing functionality both from the old apps and from the website.
I am not sure how important my own gripes are as a power user, perhaps in the end it will be better for new users, but it sort of feels like iNaturalists goals as an organization may not be as aligned with the original charter as they once were. For the purposes of financial stability it is probably most important to grow

I use Google Calendar heavily, averaging ~10 entries per day for the last 5+ years, and then some entries per day all the way back to when it was launched.
I can put information in easily enough, and with a few IFTTT recipes I'm able to treat Google Calendar not just as a schedule for upcoming events, appointments and reminders, but as a historical log of everything I've done. It is a time based database of my life... a diary.
I've automated my diary taking into Google Calendar. The what, where and when of everything ends up in one of 12 calendars (each calendar is effectively a label to categorise a whole group of events that have occurred).
And it's brilliant.
Except for the search.
It's really difficult to get the information back out. If I search for something I know that has happened, or has happened frequently, Google will delightfully tell me that I have matched 200 results, and then show me a list of 9 or 10 of them, with no way to paginate the remainder or search the old ones (it only finds upcoming, not past).
Search is broken on Google Calendar, to the point of being almost totally useless.
Far better to rely on time as a search dimension and jump around dates until one manually finds whatever you were looking for. It's that broken.
Compare to search on a product that has some love: Google Photos. Where now the miraculous occurs, I can search things like "Felicity skiing" and what will return are photos of my wife skiing, and an option to look at all other photos on those days. A simple search and all the results you want, and a single click to expand to view it in the wider context that makes sense.
Google Calendar really needs a decent search. It feels far too much like writing to /dev/null at the moment. Your information went in there, but the chances of you finding it when you wish to reference it are pretty non-existent.

(I've been doing a TON of cleaning of my office and being able to get rid of old documents by scanning them to Evernote is great) Nothing else fully replicates all the features Evernote has: OCR of images/PDFs/etc., email to new note, literally the best web clipper, connect to calendar and create/link notes to events, go to note/tag/notebook, etc. It's not the fastest app out there, but generally pretty consistent no matter how much I throw at it. The approach noted in this article is similar to an experience I just had.
I recently had some old hardware manuals I wanted to digitize, which were pages in 3-ring binders. I started thinking about scanning them but did not have an auto-loading, xerox style scanner at home. I looked around for free software that could do this 'google books style' as they did here in this article - take a photo of each page and automatically find the corners, dewarp, white balance, etc. and export to PDF.
I actually didn't find a premade solution that looked like what I wanted. So I wrote my own, with Python an a simple tk GUI.
I tried a lot Open CV messing about to do automatic page corner detection and whatnot, but found everything I tried unreliable. Sure, the corners may autodetect about 95% of the time, but if 5% of the pages fail and get cropped wrong or dewarped weird, I noted the time it took to go back and fix those errors eclipsed the time saved by the entire rest of the automatic process.
The fastest method I found was a human in the loop semi-auto program: it loaded in all the images from SD card, and had the user manually click the 4-corners of the page as shown in the image. Upon the 4th point being clicked, the page would auto-de-perspective and apply the last saved default white balance curve, thresholding, and posterizing (color binning) / grayscaling / scaling to fixed width. For subsequent images in the camera roll this meant settings didn't have to usually be changed on a per-image basis. Then just a spacebar to add the image to the saved temp queue and at the end an export to PDF.
This approach had me digitizing about 600 pages in an hour I estimate. Yes, it was a lot of clicking for the manual part.... but it allowed me to proof every page as it flew by and this caught a few photographic errors that I wouldn't have caught if it was fully automated, and not a single page was left mis-shapen or unreadable.

I'm a backend infrastructure guy rather than a product guy so I'll do my best but please take it all with a large grain of salt. I was privy to some of the higher-level discussions, but I spend most of my days down in the guts of the system. I don't spend much time debating the finer points of product direction or user experience (and the world is probably a better place because of that!)
Conceptually, Google Photos is very much a V1 product. It might sound a little weird since the team is experienced and a lot of the technology it is built on has been through multiple iterations.
But from a _product perspective_ Google Photos is a new product.
The product team was really focused on a few key aspects of the user experience (I'm not going to try to enumerate them here. The main reason is that I would certainly do a poor job of explaining them. The other reasons are that I can't remember how much of the strategy has been talked about publicly and it doesn't really matter for the point I'm trying to make).
Being focused meant saying no to things - at least for the initial launch.
So the first answer to your question is that for most of the mentioned features the answer is that they simply didn't make the cut for V1. I can't comment on which features will or won't make it to future versions.
Date picker is an interesting one. Really, the only reason it existed was to work around how painful it was access older pictures in Google+ Photos, Date picker was added to (somewhat) ease that pain.
In building a new product, there was a desire to make things like date-picker unnecessary. Make finding older photos so fast and painless that you don't even need it. Try grabbing the scroll bar in the new web-app - you can scroll to any time you want in seconds. On mobile, it's easy to zoom out, scroll and zoom back in.
There is also search, which often means you don't even _need_ to scroll through your photos to find what you want. Just this morning my wife wanted me to find a picture of a tatoo from six years ago. I was able to find it by searching for tatoo. It was awesome! In Google+ Photos I would have spent a long time trying to figure out the right date range and then searching around.
If you really want to jump to a date, just type it in search - I just tried "September 2012" and "9/23/2012" and they both worked great.
So I would argue that date-picker just flat out isn't needed any more, because the team focused on some core user experience flows.

I worked at Google a long time ago now during the whole Google+ fiasco. One thing that was super controversial internally was the so-called Real Names policy. For those who don't know or remember, it was Vic Gundotra's idea that people should use their real identities. He kept using this weird example that he didn't want it filled with people named "Dog Turd". I don't know why.
So there was this mysterious black box that decided if your name was "real" or not. At first this didn't support pseudonyms or any kind of anonymity and that's actually really important for any social network. Think of someone seeking help coming to terms with their sexual orientation, gender identity, addiction, eating disorder or whatever. Or simply going against their family's religious wishes. I later worked at Facebook and one thing I'll give them credit for is Groups. FB Groups had an identity that actually couldn't be tied by anyone else to your profile or identity in any other group. That was a good product decision.
Anyway, if your name somehow failed the magic real names filter, your account got banned. Your entire Google account was banned and basically there was no recourse other than knowing someone who worked at the company or making a big enough fuss on Twitter.
Many people, myself included, criticized and protested this decision. You should at least segment Google products. There's absolutely no reason to ban your Gmail account because an automated system decided your Google+ account name wasn't "real". But that feedback was ignored and this was well before the public launch. And the public backlash proved this position correct (IMHO).
But the net effect was that I decided I can't use any other Google product. Let's say a system is launched to find offensive photos and there's a false positive on one of my images in Google Photos. Maybe it's just a hash collision with a known image. And then what? I lose my entire Gmail? Are you kidding me?
It's wild to me that this is still an issue ~15 years later. I think my stance actually isn't strict enough anymore. You probably shouldn't use Gmail at all. I should really find a paid email provider hosted entirely in Europe, preferably Switzerland or some other country with strong pro-user regulation.
So I have no idea if this Gemini story is true or not. I say that because 95% of the things on Reddit are completely made up. But it is plausible. I wouldn't be surprised if it's true. It means I wouldn't use Gemini at all if I used Gmail.

Have you tried using the Files app for image/file transfers? You can add Samba (and other) shares in there by tapping the '...' in the upper-right corner, hitting 'Connect to Server', then inputting your local server's address and connecting. I use this not just for photos, but for transferring various files and docs to/from my phone/home server.
You mentioned not wanting to mass-select 2000+ photos. If the photos you're uploading fall within a certain date range, you can open the Photos app, search for the date range of photos you want to upload (e.g. "April 20 2024 to today", or "sept 21 2018 to mar 2020"). It'll return photos taken in that date range, where you can tap 'See All', then 'Select' > 'Select All' at the top of the screen. Then you can hit the 'Share' dialogue and upload to your server through Files without having to scroll and select tons of individual pics. Keep in mind that you can't use a '-' in place of the word 'to' when specifying a date range for some reason.
If your images are family memories, you might be interested in Immich[1] (if you're open to making changes to your photo storage setup). Stand up and configure the local server, install the smartphone app, enable automatic sync, and it'll automatically upload new photos from your phone when you open the Immich app. No need for you to manually keep track of your photo syncs. Built to be a local Google Photos replacement. Has features like shared albums, face recognition/person naming, smart search, etc. AI tasks, like everything else, are done entirely locally. It's a nice piece of software, and lots of people (including privacy advocate Louis Rossmann) vouch for it.
[1] https://immich.app/

> The downside of that is that your ability to find a specific picture from 5 years ago is entirely restricted to the extent that you were able to organize and add specific metadata to that picture.
I disagree with the premise that we should spend time manually organizing and tagging our pictures all that much.
The metadata that the phone adds to pictures – time stamp and GPS coordinates – is already sufficient in a lot of cases for finding pictures that I look for.
And where that metadata is insufficient, improved search powered by machine learning will come to the rescue. And not just tomorrow but even today.
Just the other day, a few weeks back, I was standing in the kitchen that I share with two other people and I wondered to myself whether the kitchen knife in the dishwasher was mine (I’d bought a new one a few days prior but couldn’t remember what it looked like). I take a lot of picture of random stuff and mundane things, most of which I never bother to organize or tag or anything. I pull up my phone, search my photo library for “knife” and lo and behold, I did take a picture of it when I bought it and my phone has recognized the object in the photo to be a knife so it was able to find it for me.
Important files and photos I do organize. Specifically for three reasons:
1. Ease of access.
2. Grouping related data together.
3. Tying photos and other data to abstract concepts like ideas for possible games or products.
So I am not advocating no organization or tagging at all.
But I think a lot of people are unaware or at least haven’t really incorporated the distinction between information that is already present in the data, and information that must be manually added. So they spend a lot of time manually creating folder structures that encode information which could already be automatically derived from the data itself.
As for messages in closed apps, I just screenshot them. And I am relying on OCR technology to be or become good enough to refind those messages in the future. For having used Memories on Nextcloud, and having spent hours trying to micro optimize the Nginx & PHP configuration, I can safely say that, while it is better than the Nextcloud’s native Photos app, this is absolutely nowhere near to Immich, Filerun, or surprisingly even a dumb SMB share (which doesn’t have thumbnail caching…!). I’ve really tried hard, as Immich’s support for external libraries was still in a PR at that time, and didn’t want to have two separate tools to grab files and grab photos.
A big part of the problem, it seems, is that, when you have a large library, and you jump/scroll to a specific year or so, it won’t cancel the previous page(s) worth of thumbnails loading. So as soon as you’re scrolling to search for something, it quickly accumulates hundreds of useless requests that quickly overload the PHP workers, and make everything crawl to a standstill.
I personally had to give up. When trying to grab photos from abroad for my shortly upcoming proposal, I’ve literally deleted Nextcloud/Memories, plopped Immich in docker compose, let it index/transcode/generate thumbnails from scratch against my “external library” (so Immich doesn’t duplicate the medias), and that ended up savings me days of buffering, and was able to find the nice pictures for the occasion!

Nice to hear from someone else with a huge iCloud Photo Library--we've got about 1.2 TB! After a lot of experimentation with Google Photos, Synology's photo APP, etc. we finally settled on going all in on the Apple ecosystem (we're an all-Apple family). The game-changer for us was when Apple finally supported shared photo libraries between users.
The ability to search the photo library has been steadily improving (in my experience, Google still has an edge over Apple in this area) and with the advent of new AI technology I only expect it to get better. Except for special occasions I don't even attempt to "organize" or "tag" my photos. It reminds me of how Google Search surpassed early 'library catalog' style indexes like Yahoo.
The biggest downside of iCloud is the lack of an API to access the data programmatically for backups etc. I've experimented with `icloudpd` and it worked OK, but I'm not sure about the long-term stability as it's basically just "screen scraping" iCloud.com to download the photos from the web which is not officially supported by Apple and is sensitive to any changes to the website as well as the (remote?) possibility of getting your account banned. The performance is also bad as it has to download all photos even the ones that are already stored locally.
There’s also `osxphotos` ( https://github.com/RhetTbull/osxphotos ) which works by reverse engineering the undocumented sqlite database in the photos library that Apple uses for storing the photos metadata. This avoids the performance problems of accessing the library through iCloud.com like `icloudp` does and enables many more features like searching by faces, places, etc. and they have an export function with a ton of options to backup your library.
Finally, I have a side-project working on a simple set-it-and-forget Mac app for backing up your entire photo library (including iCloud Photos) to a local disk, network share, NAS, etc. Unlike the above options, it uses the official Apple PhotoKit library to access the photos and doesn’t require setting up a Python environment, running command-line tools, etc. If you’re interested check it out here: https://www.ibeni.net

Folder-based photo management software for local use. You'd think that there is more than enough photo management software out there. But for quite a while now, I have struggled to find Mac software suitable for my requirements. The management software will be used on normal everyday pictures (holidays, landscapes and so on) as well as a large collection of documentary pictures with little artistic value from renovating protected old buildings. Working with those documentary pictures will require extensive tagging and search functions. I don't strictly require built-in editing and raw conversion functions. My requirements list: Native Mac program (or at least very well ported interface from a different OS) Pictures must be stored in a folder structure on disk, not a monolithic catalogue This folder structure must follow changes made within the software, and any changes made in Finder must be tracked and represented in the photo manager The manager must be able to write geotags, textual tags and timestamp corrections directly into the images (in order to make the metadata available to 3rd party apps -- sidecar files like those used by Darktable are useless there) Geotags must be viewable on a map Metadata and changes to the image catalogs must be easily syncable using classic, non-cloud tools like rsync, unison, Bittorrent Sync or SyncThing. Bonus points for: support of other operating system hierarchical tags user-definable integration of external editing tools Apart from KDE's really great DigiKam , which suffers from a not-yet-perfect Mac port, I did not find any software fulfilling those rather simple requirements. Perhaps someone here can point out what I missed. I evaluated the following programs: Digikam . Great. It's just heavily using the KDE ecosystem, which makes building the port on a Mac hard. It's also badly integrated in the OSX desktop. Aperture . That's what I'm currently using. Syncing catalogues between machines using rsync is not trivial. Managed libraries don't properly follow changes done in Finder. Tagging is unnecessarily complicated. Lyn . Small, lean, Mac only. Rather rudimentary. Doesn't fulfil requirement 4. Darktable . See no. 4 above -- sidecar approaches are impractical for me, and " darktable will never ever open source files for writing ". Capture One . Fails on point 3, and the support told me that syncing between machines should only be done through manual import/export of sessions. Media Pro . Same as above. Unbound . Very rudimentary. No external tools configurable. Needs Dropbox as sync backend. Pixa . Seems to be developed only very slowly, which does not make me feel good about its longevity. Doesn't really seem like photo management, but rather more like digital asset management. No geotagging. Apple Photos / Google Photos. Cloud based. Too rudimentary. Edit: November 2019 additions Skylum Luminar 4 . Represents the folder-based structure on disk perfectly in its DAM component. Offers flexible plugin manage
